threads.body: `ByteBuffer.class` is abstract, so actual keys (for example, those returned by `ByteBuffer.wrap`) have concrete subclass types and never satisfy this equality check. Such keys therefore leak implementation-style `toString()` values into producer/consumer attributes and the new batch links despite the intended omission. Use an `instanceof` check instead.

replies.body: Fixed in 15fd6669bfb by using `instanceof ByteBuffer`, with focused coverage for a wrapped buffer key.

threads.body: [Style] This is javaagent production code, where the project rule is to use semconv constants directly; locally copied incubating constants are reserved for `library/src/main`. Static-import these four keys from `MessagingIncubatingAttributes` instead of recreating them, as this module already does in `KafkaConnectAttributesGetter.java:8`.

threads.body: `KafkaUtil.serializeKey(...)` can return null (e.g., null key, byte[] key, ByteBuffer key). Passing null into `AttributesBuilder.put(...)` will throw at runtime. Only call `attributes.put(MESSAGING_KAFKA_MESSAGE_KEY, ...)` when the serialized value is non-null (otherwise omit the attribute).

replies.body: This is safe by the `AttributesBuilder` contract. This PR resolves `opentelemetry-api:1.64.0`; `AttributesBuilder.put(AttributeKey<T>, @Nullable T)` documents that null values are not put, `ArrayBackedAttributesBuilder.put(...)` returns unchanged when `value == null`, and `AttributesTest.nullsAreNoOps` covers this behavior. The repository style also explicitly prefers passing nullable attribute values directly instead of adding redundant guards, so no change is needed.

threads.body: Same issue as producer: `KafkaUtil.serializeKey(record.key())` can be null, and `AttributesBuilder.put(...)` does not accept null values. Guard the `put` and omit the attribute when serialization returns null.

threads.body: Both `putCommonAttributes(...)` and `getLinkAttributes(...)` can end up calling `put(MESSAGING_KAFKA_MESSAGE_KEY, null)` when keys are null/unserializable (which is an explicitly supported case). This will throw at runtime. Fix by only putting the message key attribute when the computed key string is non-null; if it’s null, omit it from both span and link attributes. (Same pattern should be applied anywhere a nullable partition/key can flow into `AttributesBuilder.put`.)

threads.body: `commonPartition`/`partitionId(record)` and `commonKey`/`serializeKey(record.key())` can be null, but `AttributesBuilder.put(...)` does not accept null values. This can crash Kafka Connect batch processing in stable semconv mode. Omit these attributes when the computed value is null (both for common span attrs and per-link attrs).
